title: SCA Minhag of the Week 275: "Shabuot: Forgotten Customs"

chapters.title: Decorating with flowers
chapters.about: Flowers and greenery in the synagogue

chapters.title: Chag HaBikkurim
chapters.about: Connection to the Beit HaMikdash and growth

chapters.title: Teaching in the vernacular
chapters.about: Using Judeo-Arabic for Azharot and Aseret HaDibrot

summary: This class explores several forgotten customs associated with the holiday of Shabuot. The teacher discusses the tradition of decorating the synagogue with flowers, the practice of sprinkling water and floral waters, the recitation of the Ketubah deChag HaShabuot, and the historical use of Judeo-Arabic texts to make the holiday messages accessible to the entire community.
questions: Why do some communities decorate the synagogue with flowers on Shabuot?
What is the connection between Shabuot and the sprinkling of water?
What was the Ketubah deChag HaShabuot?
Why were texts like the Azharot and Mishle translated into Judeo-Arabic?
How can we bring the messages of Shabuot home today?
